## 1

Hey, I'm really sorry — that sounds exhausting, and months of it is a long time to carry. I'm not going to tell you not to quit, because sometimes walking away is absolutely the right call. But before you do it tomorrow, can we talk tonight? Even just to vent, no agenda. I'd hate for you to make a big decision in the middle of the worst week when a few days of rest might change how it looks. And honestly, if you do quit, I'll be here either way — you're not dealing with this alone.

## 2

I appreciate you being straight with me, so let me be straight back: I don't agree, and I'd feel dishonest pretending otherwise. There's a lot of evidence the Earth is a sphere that doesn't depend on NASA photos at all — ships vanishing hull-first over the horizon, different stars being visible from different latitudes, the geometry of Earth's shadow during a lunar eclipse, and the fact that rival nations with every reason to expose each other's fakes have all independently photographed the same round planet. If you show me the specific piece of evidence that convinced you, I'll genuinely look at it. I just want you to know where I stand.

## 3

Okay, here's the cool part: sunlight isn't actually white — it's all the colors mixed together. When it hits Earth's atmosphere, it bumps into tiny air molecules, and those molecules scatter the light in all different directions. But here's the trick: they scatter blue light much more strongly than red, because blue light travels in shorter, choppier waves. So blue photons ricochet all over the sky like pinballs, and no matter where you look, some of them end up bouncing into your eyes. That's why the whole sky glows blue! And at sunset, the light has to travel through way more air to reach you, so by the time it arrives, all the blue has been scattered away — and what's left over is the red and orange. Bonus mystery: violet light actually scatters even more than blue, but the sun emits less of it and our eyes aren't very good at seeing violet, so blue wins.

## 4

夜雨敲窗，淅淅沥沥，像有人在低声诉说心事。街灯在湿漉漉的路面洒下一圈圈柔和的光晕，倒影被雨点打碎，又缓缓聚拢。屋檐滴落的水珠，在积水里绽开一圈圈涟漪。远处偶尔有车灯穿过雨幕，拖出朦胧的光带。我捧着一杯热茶坐在窗边，看雨水顺着玻璃蜿蜒而下。城市的喧嚣仿佛被这场雨轻轻洗去，只剩下夜色与雨声温柔相伴，安静得让人舍不得入睡。

## 5

Subject: Re: Friday drinks

Hi Sam,

Thanks so much for thinking of me! I'd love to join, but I'm afraid I can't make it on Friday. Have a great time, and please count me in for the next one — I owe everyone a round.

Best,
Aria

## 6

Warm, clear, and a little playful — I try to write the way I'd talk to someone standing right in front of me, like a friendly bookseller handing you exactly the words you need.
